PRICE PRIORS for recurring line types (statistical model fitted on the thresholds t revealed
in earlier games; gross amounts). How to use them:
- The amounts are final thresholds as they were revealed: they already contain whatever
  deductible, VAT and customary-price judgement applied in those cases, and they were computed
  from the full invoiced quantity (the whole quantity was indemnified there). For an
  indemnified line of this type take the stated amount for the line as t as it stands and give
  a price_log_sd that matches the stated range. Do not deduct a deductible from it and do not
  cut the invoiced quantity.
- Deviate only for something this case has and those cases did not: an aggregate cap or
  sub-limit that the lines of this invoice must share, a percentage reduction for a breached
  duty, or a purchase price or sum insured stated in the claim that limits the line.
- Whether a line is indemnified in THIS case is decided by the policy and the claim, not by
  the history. The history only says how often this line type was paid at all. A line type
  that was never indemnified before is usually an ancillary charge the policies do not carry;
  treat it as indemnified only if this policy clearly says so.

items.rationale: The theft-damaged frame is covered at the cost of a like-for-like replacement under §§2.3.1 and 7.1.7(b). The €3,500 agreed value replaces the €500 class cap under §4.4, so the estimated €850 gross frame cost is not reduced.
The brakes were damaged during the theft, so §§7.1.7(b) and 7.1.9 allow €180 gross for a set matching the pre-loss specification, without an upgrade allowance.

Section 7.1.7(f) expressly covers necessary freight for covered replacement parts. Allow €25 gross for one shipment, provided it is attributable to the repair and does not duplicate another transport charge.
Sections 7.1.7(f)–(g) and 7.1.8(f)–(g) allow necessary repair transport or attendance, but not duplicate or unnecessary trips. Allow €77 gross for one distinct, necessary trip if documented.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers fitting and aligning the replacement frame and brakes. Allow €109 gross for the assembly work, excluding any labour already billed separately.
Section 7.1.7(e) permits a grouped charge for small parts and consumables used in the covered repair. Allow €15 gross if the charge is tied to that work rather than workshop overhead.
Section 7.1.7(d) expressly allows separately stated apprentice time needed for the repair. One hour at €36 gross is allowable if not already included in assembly.
Sections 7.1.7(d) and 7.1.8(g) allow necessary skilled labour at customary rates, but not time already charged under assembly. Allow one distinct hour at €80 gross.
Section 5.2.2(a) covers the locksmith's necessary attendance at the recovery site. Allow €40 gross, in line with the comparable locksmith visit in Case 23; the €1,000 recovery cap does not reduce it.
Under §§5.2.2(b) and 7.1.10, this charge is assessed by its purpose: cutting and removing the seized lock to release the bicycle. Allow €109 gross for that operation, excluding labour billed twice.
Section 5.2.2(b) covers materials consumed in releasing the bicycle, not a generic tool or overhead charge. Allow €8 gross if the line represents actual lock-removal consumables.
Section 5.2.2(b) covers necessary recovery labour of every grade. Allow €36 gross for one apprentice hour, consistent with Case 23, provided it is not included in the operation charge.

Section 5.2.2(b) covers skilled labour needed to release the bicycle, while §7.1.8(g) bars billing the same work twice. If this hour is distinct from the flat operation charge, estimate €44 gross using Case 23.
